title: Today in one sentence
text: Friday was a rough day for tech: the S&P 500 fund SPY fell 1.1% and the Nasdaq 100 fund QQQ fell 2.5% while defense stock Lockheed Martin rose 3.7%; over the weekend, think about how many of your eggs sit in one basket, and on Monday watch whether chip stocks keep sliding or settle.

title: Chip stocks had their worst day in weeks
text: AMD fell 6.0%, Broadcom 4.5%, Vertiv 3.9% and TSMC 2.3% on Friday. Rocket Lab dropped 8.0%, the biggest fall on our list. These companies make or support the hardware behind AI, so they tend to move together when investors get worried about AI.

title: Defense and dividend funds held steady
text: Lockheed Martin rose 3.7%, the dividend fund SCHD rose 0.7% and GE Aerospace rose 0.6%. When tech falls, money often moves to steadier areas. That does not mean they always win, only that different industries often act differently on the same day.

title: Lockheed reports on October 22
text: Lockheed Martin reports quarterly results before the market opens on Thursday, October 22. Report days often bring big moves, so it is a good chance to see how a company's real numbers affect its stock, up or down.

title: Interest rates are the big worry
text: The 10 year Treasury yield is near 5.1%, and hot inflation news this week makes another Fed rate hike more likely at the end of October. Higher rates make borrowing costlier and make safe bonds more attractive, which can weigh on stocks.

title: Lesson 11: What is position sizing?
text: Position sizing means deciding how much money goes into each investment. Imagine you have $1,000 and put all of it in one stock that then drops 8% in a day, like Rocket Lab did today. You lose $80. If you had put only $100 in it, you would lose just $8. The riskier a stock swings, the smaller the slice many investors choose, so one bad day cannot hurt the whole plan. This is not advice to buy or sell anything; it is a way to think about how much any single idea matters to your total.
